text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- State Secretary Elemer Kiss announced Thursday that the cabinet will submit a bill amending the law on social insurance contributions that was introduced on January 1. @

- NATO Secretary General Javier Solana, who again made a stopover in Budapest on his way back from Ankara to Brussels, was less sure on Thursday about whether Turkey would veto the eastward enlargement of the military alliance.

- More than 12 persons are being nominated for the post of Free Democrat parliamentary group leader ahead of this Sunday's election, however, incumbent Ivan Peto appears to be the only candidate for the post since most nominees have rejected their nominations. @

- Smallholder president Jozsef Torgyan said his party is willing to conclude a preliminary agreement with those conservative parties that agree to step back in favour of the most successful candidate in the second round of elections.
- The Finance Ministry has begun an investigation into former activities of Polgari Bank and the reason and consequences of losses incurred last year.
- Police have captured the man responsible for Tuesday's gas explosion in a 12th district flat in Budapest and revealed that the blast was ignited with a timing device.
NEPSZABADSAG @
- The government finance deficit was 3.3 percent last year, as compared to the targeted 4 percent, said Finance Ministry deputy state secretary Csaba Laszlo.
- Wine producers plan to close half of the lanes on roads in Bacs-Kiskun, Csongrad and Szolnok counties on February 14 to protest against new social insurance and tax regulations.

- The nation's pig stock stood at 5.289 million on December. The live cattle stock stood at 900,000 in early December, of which cows made up 400,000. The former figure is the lowest since World War II.
MAGYAR HIRLAP @

- Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar yesterday told Parliament that Hungarians are the only ethnic minority in Slovakia who want a minority language law and declared that rumours about a pledge to draw up a minority language law are wrong.

- The HUF 360 billion deficit of government finances projected this year and the renewal of HUF 1,400 billion in state debts this year requires a bigger financing requirement than last year. To meet this, the State Debt Management Centre plans to issue state securities to a total value of HUF 1,800 billion. @
- Another 80-100 shares are expected to be introduced onto the Budapest Stock Exchange in the next three years.
- The privatisation of Magyar Hitel Bank was fully completed on Thursday, when the HUF 2.4 billion state guarantee for the bank's bad debts arrived at the bank's account.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Nobody bought Globus shares during their first day in the free trading category of the Frankfurt Stock Exchange yesterday. @
- Raffeisen Unicbank had pre-tax profits of HUF 7.391 billion last year according to non-audited figures released yesterday.
- Porcelain manufacturer Zsolnay closed last year with net sales of HUF 1.9 billion and pre-tax profits of about HUF 52 million.
